notes: IFRS in every year FY2007-FY2025 (Heineken moved to IFRS in 2005), so no standard change inside the period.

revenue is net revenue, i.e. after excise tax expense. From FY2016 Heineken also presents gross revenue (FY2025: net 28,753m vs gross 34,257m); the net figure is the one used here and the one data vendors report.

operatingIncome is "Results from operating activities" (FY2007-FY2016 statements) / "Operating profit" (FY2017-FY2025). Heineken also reports "operating profit (beia)", a non-IFRS measure (FY2025: 4,385m); that is deliberately not used.

totalDebt = non-current borrowings + current borrowings. For FY2007-FY2016 "Bank overdrafts and commercial papers" was a separate line inside current liabilities and is included here; from FY2016 the balance sheet presents cash gross and the overdrafts sit inside current borrowings.

cashAndEquivalents is the balance-sheet "Cash and cash equivalents" line. From FY2016 it is gross of bank overdrafts; the cash-flow statement closing cash is net of them and is lower (e.g. FY2015: 3,232m vs 282m). The gross-up (IAS 7 amendment) also restated FY2015 total assets from 37,714m to 40,122m.
capex = purchase of property, plant and equipment + purchase of intangible assets, stored negative.

Each year is read from the annual report that contains it as the most recent published figure: FY2025 and FY2024 from the 2025 report, and each earlier year from the following year report comparative column where that report restated it (see restated flags), otherwise from its own report -- FY2007 from the 2008 report.

restated=true: FY2007 (accounting policy change, AR2008 note 3(b)); FY2008 (finalisation of the Scottish & Newcastle purchase-price allocation, AR2009, total assets 20,563 -> 20,587); FY2010 (IAS 19 employee benefits, AR2011: operating profit 2,283 -> 2,298, net profit 1,436 -> 1,447, total assets 26,549 -> 26,662, equity 10,228 -> 9,932); FY2012 (revised IAS 19, AR2013: operating profit 3,691 -> 3,697, net profit 2,949 -> 2,914, equity 11,691 -> 11,734); FY2015 (cash gross-up, AR2016); FY2017 (IFRS 15, AR2018: revenue 21,888 -> 21,609 and debt re-presented, 15,513 -> 15,378); FY2018 (IAS 37, AR2019: net revenue 22,471 -> 22,489, operating profit 3,137 -> 3,121, net profit 1,903 -> 1,913, total assets 41,956 -> 42,151, equity 14,358 -> 14,525).

source.page points to the consolidated primary statements (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow) of the cited report. dividendPerShare comes from the five-year summary of the same report (AR2025 PDF p. 276; AR2016 PDF p. 166 for the 2012-2016 series) and sharesOutstanding from the share-capital / own-shares disclosure of the same report (AR2025 PDF p. 272; AR2016 PDF p. 161).

FY2008 is read from the KU Leuven library copy of the official Heineken N.V. Annual Report 2008; the company-hosted PDF for that year could not be retrieved. The document is the company published report, only the host differs.

employees = average number of employees, FTE (as published). The pre-2012 reports give headcount instead (AR2011 quotes 64,252 for 2011); FY2011 here uses the FTE basis restated in the 2012 report (71,745) so the series is consistent from FY2011 on.

sharesOutstanding = shares outstanding at 31 December excluding own shares (FY2025: 560,557,296 shares of EUR 1.60 nominal). The count steps from 489,974,594 to 576,002,613 in 2010 because of the rights issue that part-funded the FEMSA beer acquisition.
dividendPerShare = total dividend proposed for the fiscal year (interim + final) in EUR per share; FY2020 was cut to 0.70 because the interim dividend was suspended.

Cross-check against docs/global-companies/snapshot-2026-10-26.json (Yahoo, USD): at the implied rates (FY2025 1.1323, FY2024 1.0802, FY2023 1.0848, FY2022 1.0517) revenue and net income agree exactly and totalAssets, totalEquity, cash, totalDebt, dilutedEPS, operatingCashFlow and capex agree to the euro-equivalent, confirming all line definitions. Yahoo operatingIncome sits 1-4% below Heineken operating profit (FY2023 3,097 vs 3,229; FY2025 3,332 vs 3,406), a difference of EBIT definition on Yahoo side, not a different Heineken line.
